background_notes.fact: For z∈[0,∞] with z≠∞, z.toReal≥0 and ofReal(z.toReal)=z. For nonnegative real a,b, ofReal a≤ofReal b iff a≤b, likewise for strict inequality, and ofReal(a+b)=ofReal a+ofReal b. Every ofReal b is finite; consequently z≤ofReal b implies z≠∞. Also 0≠∞ and ∞≤z implies z=∞.

background_notes.justification: The extended nonnegative reals consist of the nonnegative reals and an added largest element infinity. On finite nonnegative values, the embedding and finite-value map are inverse and the order and addition are the real ones. A finite embedded value is strictly below infinity, so a value bounded by it cannot be infinity. Top-element antisymmetry gives the last implication. These facts justify the initial identification and subsequent finite-value comparisons and addition; S004 establishes product finiteness before applying the finite inverse there.

background_notes.justification: Nonnegativity and symmetry hold in each coordinate; distance zero forces both coordinates equal. Each coordinate distance obeys the triangle inequality and is bounded by the maximum on its corresponding leg, so both coordinate distances across a triangle are bounded by the sum of the two leg maxima; taking their maximum proves the product triangle inequality. Embedding the nonnegative metric distances gives the extended metric inequalities. The sigma algebra generated by this metric's open sets is its Borel structure by construction; no product-sigma-algebra identification or measurability of G is needed.
